ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and on all trigger events against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, OFAC non-SDN sanctions, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, United Kingdom HM Treasury sanctions, the South African targeted financial sanctions list issued under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004, and FIC-imposed financial sanctions directives. PEP screening must identify domestic and foreign prominent public officials, their immediate family members and close associates; any PEP match requires enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and, where applicable, source-of-funds verification. The compliance file must record the screening method, match results, decision rationale and the date of refresh.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices Portal, Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any of the eleven official languages of South Africa using the Latin alphabet. Names derived from non-Latin scripts must be transliterated or romanized for the CIPC register, and the English or Afrikaans transliteration must be sufficiently distinctive to avoid confusion. A private company name must end with the mandatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd' or '(Proprietary) Limited', and the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, offensive, or misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may apply to CIPC for an extension of a name reservation before expiry through the eServices portal using the prescribed CIPC form. If CIPC rejects a proposed name, the applicant may first file administrative representations and an amended name application through CIPC eServices within the period stated in the rejection notice. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a review of the name decision, and may thereafter institute judicial review proceedings in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this low-risk, unlicensed die-casting and collectibles entity, provided the virtual-office provider maintains a genuine physical street address in South Africa, accepts service of legal process, receives and scans correspondence, and is not merely a post-office box or postnet address. The registered office must be capable of receiving service and must be recorded with CIPC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at less than five percent probability in the first operating year for an unlicensed, low-risk scale-model manufacturer. Unannounced CIPC or FIC verification is nevertheless possible if the beneficial-ownership filing is incomplete, a sanctions or PEP trigger arises, or the registered-office address clusters with entities exhibiting shell-company indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Acts 16 and 17 of 2023; ss 13-19 (incorporation), s 40 (consideration for shares), s 50 (authorised shares), ss 66-70 (board governance), s 186 (CIPC functions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, Pretoria, South Africa - e-Services / BizPortal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation on the prescribed CoR 15.1A template
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital, capitalisation, or escrow deposit rule applies under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; a Pty Ltd may be incorporated with a single nominal-value or no-par subscriber share, provided the share is fully subscribed and the agreed consideration is paid or recorded at incorporation in terms of s 40.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION no. 1 (adopted 3rd day, 2025 year): 1) The allotment of 100 no-par ordinary shares to the founding subscribers, fully paid in cash, is approved and recorded in the securities register. 2) The registered office is established at 14 Foundry Industrial Park, Cullinan, Gauteng, South Africa, and CIPC is notified. 3) The board is constituted; [Managing Director] is appointed Managing Director, [Financial Director] Financial Director, and [Public Officer] Company Secretary and SARS Public Officer, authorised to open bank accounts, procure licences, and execute tax registrations. 4) This resolution is effective immediately. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CoR 9.1 on the CIPC BizPortal proposing up to two preferred company names; the automated registry screens for identical, confusingly similar, or prohibited names under ss 11-12 of the Companies Act and Regulation 14 of the Companies Regulations; once cleared, a name reservation certificate valid for six months is issued.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (name reservation application)
Certified identity document or passport of the submitting director
Written consent of any natural person or legal entity whose name appears in the proposed company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, obtain the written CIPC grounds of refusal, re-file with a new distinctive name, or lodge a name objection and alternative-name application within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory incorporation filing and registration certificate issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) and the executed Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A) via the CIPC BizPortal; pay the statutory filing fee electronically; after s 14 compliance screening, CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) reflecting the company registration number, date of incorporation, and issued share capital.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
Form CoR 15.1A Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents or passports of all incorporators and initial directors
Written consents of appointed directors and any company secretary or auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or Notice of Non-Compliance, correct the s 14 statutory particulars and re-file within 10 business days to prevent rejection or deregistration under s 17; any correction tariff is payable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS tax registration and public officer appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal and SARS branch offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on SARS eFiling for Income Tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy; appoint a SARS Public Officer resident in South Africa in terms of s 246 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; register for VAT when taxable turnover equals or exceeds R1 million per annum, with voluntary registration permitted from R50,000.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Proof of registered office address and local bank account confirmation
Identity documents of directors and appointee Public Officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address SARS verification requests (ITR/RFL) by uploading rectified supporting documents on eFiling; request a SARS compliance status pin and escalate unresolved queries through the SARS branch dispute desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate banking mandate and FICA due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank (e.g., Standard Bank, First National Bank) - Corporate and Business Banking divisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, authorising board resolution, and FICA documentation pack to open a corporate business account; the bank screens all beneficial owners and directors for KYC/AML compliance; request Swift-wire and PayPal cross-border settlement rails for export-oriented die-cast collectible trade.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
FICA documents for directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners (identity, residential and business address proof)
Board resolution authorising account opening and signatories
Source-of-funds declaration for initial paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a FICA/KYC query, submit enhanced due diligence records such as source-of-wealth vouchers, capital contribution receipts, and organisational charts; if deferred, re-apply at a second tier-1 bank with the completed FICA pack.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DOEL) - UIF and Compensation Fund registries (eComply portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the DOEL employer registration application to obtain a UIF reference number and a Compensation Fund employer number; integrate those numbers into the monthly PAYE/SDL wage remittance cycle; maintain a Letter of Good Standing for future tenders, bank covenants, and immigration sponsor applications.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
SARS PAYE employer registration number
Identity documents of the employer and payroll mandate holder
Company bank account verification and letterhead
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate dormant registration files to the provincial DOEL office; alternatively, re-submit the registration via eComply with the SARS tax reference number as a cross-check to force processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance, beneficial ownership filing, and annual return readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Registry and Annual Returns Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, keep the MOI, securities register, minute books, and beneficial ownership records at the registered office; file the CIPC beneficial ownership declaration identifying every beneficial owner holding 5 percent or more of the shares; thereafter lodge the first annual return on the company's anniversary in terms of s 33 of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Securities register showing subscriber share allotments
Minutes of the first board and shareholder resolutions
Beneficial ownership declaration forms and supporting ownership structure chart
CIPC annual return statutory forms (e-services template)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual return deadlines are missed, apply to CIPC for a late-filing exemption or administrative rectification under s 26; update the beneficial ownership register within 10 business days of any shareholding change to avoid administrative penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) - Industrial Manufacturing Branch; Municipal Business Licensing Department of the City of Ekurhuleni / City of Tshwane for the Cullinan industrial site
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Operating Licence for the manufacturing of die-cast scale model vehicles under the Business Licensing Act, 1991 (Act 71 of 1991) and applicable Gauteng municipal by-laws; complemented by an Atmospheric Emission Licence under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 where the zinc-melting furnace meets the s 21 listed-activity threshold.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) - Environmental Impact Assessment and Licensing Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Basic Assessment tier: small-scale zinc die-casting below 100 tonnes per annum typically requires a basic assessment or a pre-application screening report under Regulation 5 of the EIA Regulations 2014 (GNR 982-985); a full Scoping and Environmental Impact Assessment Report is triggered where production capacity exceeds 100 tonnes per annum or the facility is located within a sensitive hydrological or protected area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Water: General Authorisation GN 665 under the National Water Act 36 of 1998 - pH 5.5-9.5, Chemical Oxygen Demand ≤75 mg/l, Total Suspended Solids ≤25 mg/l, zinc ≤5 mg/l. Air: furnace stack particulate matter ≤10 mg/Nm3 under the Atmospheric Emission Licence, with VOC controls on tampo-printing solvents and compliance with National Ambient Air Quality Standards; waste: zinc dross and slag classified under the Waste Classification and Management Regulations, GN 634 of 23 August 2013, and transported by a registered waste carrier with a controlled waste manifest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Compliance Certificate from the provincial Fire Services under the Fire Brigade Services Act 99 of 1987; structural engineer load certificate for the furnace platform, factory roof, and storage racking; Electrical Installation Certificate of Compliance issued by an accredited inspection authority; Compensation Fund Letter of Good Standing; and an Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 hazard communication file addressing zinc fume, dust exposure, molten-metal burn risks, and emergency evacuation drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — administered through the SARS eFiling web portal (https://efiling.sars.gov.za) and the SARS Customs eFiling system for customs and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-controlled Pty Ltd must first be incorporated with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain its company registration number. The entity must then register as a South African taxpayer with SARS to obtain a SARS tax reference number, which is the statutory tax identification number for South African companies. Registration is completed via SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch, and the company must appoint a South African-resident public officer. Once the compulsory VAT threshold is met, a separate VAT registration application is made using Form VAT 101; foreign suppliers of electronic services must use the SARS foreign-vendor registration channel where their South African supplies exceed the statutory threshold. The assessed VAT vendor number and the taxpayer profile are then recorded in the SARS RAV registered-details system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a South African Pty Ltd is a separate taxpaying entity subject to corporate income tax at 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023. Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident and branch operations are taxed on South African source income only. South African law does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for proprietary limited companies, and no tax-exempt zone designation applies to die-cast scale model manufacturing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections for a qualifying Pty Ltd include: (1) Small Business Corporation election under section 12E of the Income Tax Act where all shareholders are natural persons; (2) Micro Business Turnover Tax election under section 48 of the Income Tax Act for qualifying micro businesses with annual turnover not exceeding ZAR 1 million; (3) VAT group registration election under section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act for connected persons; (4) section 11D research and development additional deduction election; and (5) hybrid financial instrument mismatch neutralisation designations under sections 8E to 8L of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) — administered by the South African Revenue Service under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, with zero-rating for exported goods and VAT refunds claimable on the VAT 201 return.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory registration where taxable supplies exceeded or are expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary VAT registration is available once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12-month period. Foreign suppliers of electronic services supplied to South African customers must register when the value of those supplies exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital-stamping regime for VAT invoices. Tax invoices must satisfy the form and content requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act and must be issued within 21 days after the date of supply; electronic tax invoices are permitted. SARS has published a SARS Digital Tax Invoice specification and an eFiling API integration framework as a step toward phased mandatory e-invoicing, initially targeting large vendors. Customs export declarations are filed electronically via SARS Customs eFiling using the SAD 500 declaration and associated EDI/API interfaces.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Movable goods — die-cast scale automotive models — are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when supplied to a non-resident and physically exported from South Africa to a destination outside the Republic within the prescribed export window, in practice 90 days from the date of supply or invoice, provided the vendor obtains and retains documentary proof of export. Zero-rating of related services, such as design, tooling, die-casting and tampo-printing performed offshore, may apply under section 11(2) of the VAT Act where the services are supplied to a non-resident, are not consumed in South Africa, and the non-resident is outside South Africa when the services are rendered. The vendor must receive payment in foreign currency or into a South African bank account in foreign currency, and export proceeds must be physically repatriated to South Africa within the statutory 180-day exchange-control window. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export supplies is claimable via the VAT 201 return, and a refund arises where input tax exceeds output tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / Form DA500) lodged via SARS Customs eFiling evidencing physical export of the goods
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing consignment to the non-resident destination
Full tax invoice issued under section 20 of the VAT Act showing the zero-rated supply and the non-resident customer details
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order or sale contract evidencing the supply to the non-resident and the commercial export terms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of foreign-currency payment from the non-resident within 180 days of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may retrospectively claw back zero-rated treatment and assess VAT at 15% plus statutory interest where the exporter fails to retain the complete documentation bundle, misses the export or 180-day foreign-currency repatriation deadline, or submits false or irregular export documentation. Under sections 222 to 226 of the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties range from 10% to 200% of the undercharged tax depending on the taxpayer's conduct, with higher ranges for substantial understatement, negligence, and intentional tax evasion. Section 59 of the VAT Act imposes additional penalties for defective invoicing and record-keeping failures. Where fraud or material non-disclosure is established, SARS is not time-barred by the standard five-year prescription period and may raise retrospective additional assessments without limitation; serious cases may also result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) exercising delegated authority under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, read with the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FIC Act).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a dual-layer convertibility framework. Current account transactions, including trade payments, service fees and dividends declared from current profits, are freely transferable through authorised dealers without prior SARB approval, subject to documentary verification and tax clearances. Capital account transactions, including share subscriptions, disinvestments, capital loan admissions and capital loan repayments, remain subject to exchange control admission and repatriation reporting rules. The ZAR is a controlled currency for regulatory purposes, and every inbound and outbound transfer is reportable to SARB via an authorised dealer. Non-resident shareholders may remit distributable profits through ordinary dividends or branch remittances, but dividends tax at 20% before treaty relief is imposed, and the paying entity must hold a tax directive/certificate and an auditor's certificate confirming realised distributable reserves. For capital disinvestment, proceeds of a share sale must be transferred through an authorised dealer and require proof of admission of the original inward transfer, such as the authorised dealer's inward remittance certificate or a FinSurv reference, to support future repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Exchange Control Manual, an exporter must ensure that the full value of exported goods is physically received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment. Proceeds may be credited to an authorised dealer-backed Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or converted to ZAR. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio; the mandatory conversion percentage is effectively 0% where the exporter maintains an eligible FCA and demonstrates genuine operational use for the foreign currency, while an exporter without an FCA must have 100% of export proceeds credited to its ZAR account upon receipt. Each export transaction must be reported to the authorised dealer on the relevant export form (e.g., Exporter's Declaration COT 1 or the SARB Excon/MEX matrix), and a commercial invoice with the correct HS tariff classification, proof of physical export (bill of lading/airwaybill) and evidence of customs clearance must support the receipt. If extended trade credit beyond 180 days is required, prior FinSurv approval is necessary.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury purposes. South African clearing, settlement and interbank systems (SAMOS, NPS, Bankserv) are accessible only to licensed banks or authorised payment service providers. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex and Payoneer are not authorised dealers under SARB FinSurv, cannot hold ZAR nostro settlement accounts, and are not able to issue a domestic ZAR bank account for the entity. They may be used only as an ancillary collection channel for low-value export orders via PayPal/Stripe, provided the funds are settled onward to a fully licensed South African bank account through a cross-border settlement partner. All inbound foreign exchange must be reported by the receiving authorised dealer to SARB. The legal durability of such EMIs is subject to FSCA payments licensing and the National Payment System Regulations on payment admission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote account opening is possible only for a South African-registered (Pty) Ltd with South African resident directors and a clean country-risk profile. For this structure, where non-resident beneficial owners and foreign trading counterparties are present, most tier-1 banks will require either a physical KYC meeting in South Africa with an executive director/signatory, or a video interview with live identity verification and a South African attorney or auditor notarising certified copies. At least one natural person with a South African residency permit and a FATCA/CRS declaration is normally required to operate the account. The bank may further require that the financial director or account signatory appear physically for activation of high-limit electronic banking, foreign exchange dealing limits, and the issuance of letters of credit or trade guarantees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder registered in a jurisdiction with increased tax or AML sensitivity, including a grey-listed or tax-haven jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart, share register, certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, three years of audited financial statements, beneficial ownership schedule, notarised and apostilled passport copies of all persons holding 25% or more, tax residence certificates, correspondent bank references, board resolution authorising account opening, and an ultimate beneficial owner sworn affidavit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or sanctions list match on a director, shareholder or beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions screening results from the bank-approved vendor, signed PEP status explanation, source-of-wealth report prepared by a licensed attorney or forensic accountant, six months of personal bank statements, and a negative-media report with documented evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared die-cast collectible manufacturing activity and the transaction profile, including credit card or online marketplace flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master procurement and sales contracts, purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, bill of lading/airwaybill samples, photographs of the die-cast production line, ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 classification statement, VAT registration certificate, SARS import/export statement, and a technical product catalogue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import of zinc alloy raw materials or tampo printing inks flagged for dual-use, customs misclassification or hazardous goods review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs bill of entry, supplier commercial invoice showing HS codes (e.g., 7901 unworked zinc, 7905 zinc plates/sheets, 3405 polishing agents), safety data sheets, declaration confirming exclusive end-use for non-defence collectible model manufacturing, ISO 9001 quality certificate, and a process flow describing casting, trimming, tampo printing and packaging.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial share capital or inbound capital injection not supported by a documented equity subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share subscription agreement, board minutes approving share issuance, SWIFT MT103 remittance with sender's reference, sending bank account holder verification, affidavit confirming beneficial ownership of funds, no-liability declaration for third-party financing, and a declaration that funds are not derived from organised crime or tax evasion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the non-resident shareholder's equity injection begins with execution of a share subscription and issuance of ordinary shares by the (Pty) Ltd. The foreign shareholder instructs its bank to effect an SWIFT MT103 credit to the South African operating ZAR account, with Field 70/72 narrative stating 'Share Capital Subscription to [Entity Name] - Foreign Direct Investment - BOP Code 1301 (equity)'. The receiving South African authorised dealer opens an inward capital import clearing path, issues an inward remittance confirmation, and reports the transaction to SARB FinSurv through the BOP/MEX reporting framework. Verification includes a current share register, board resolution, shareholder bank account title evidence, the entity's tax reference number, FICA/AML beneficial ownership declaration, and CRS/FATCA self-certification. Where the injection is structured as a shareholder loan rather than equity, a Foreign Loan Admission procedure must be executed through the authorised dealer if the loan carries interest and a term exceeding one year, with a written loan agreement on commercial terms and, where required, FinSurv economic testing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border supplier payments, the entity should use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for routine and moderate-value purchase orders, and SWIFT-backed irrevocable documentary letters of credit (MT700/MT710) for high-value bulk purchases of zinc alloy, inks, tooling or packaging materials. Commercial LCs are issued by South African trade finance desks under UCP 600, may be confirmed by a top-tier offshore bank, and require presentation of the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airwaybill, insurance certificate, certificate of origin and, where applicable, third-party inspection certificate. Documentation must align with the SARS Customs declaration and the underlying import contract. For profit, management fee or shareholder loan interest disbursements, the entity must effect an outbound MT103 through an authorised dealer supported by a SARS tax directive or dividends tax certificate, an auditor's certificate of distributable retained earnings, and a FinSurv inward investment report proving capital admission. All FX conversions for settlement must be executed through the authorised dealer's FX desk at the prevailing spot or contracted forward rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Authorised dealer vanilla forward exchange contracts (FECs) for firm current account obligations generated by export receivables in USD, EUR or GBP and import payables for zinc alloy, inks and components; tenor normally up to 12 months, requires underlying invoice, LC or pro-forma contract.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for a long-term shareholder loan or capital equipment financing, where interest and principal repatriation flows are exchange-control admitted and the swap is executed through a SARB authorised dealer.

European-style FX options (call/put) transacted with an authorised dealer for specific trade flows or bid/order exposure; premiums and any net settlement are payable in ZAR or foreign currency as permitted by the authorised dealer.
Long-dated forwards for commodity-linked procurement contracts (e.g., tonne-based zinc alloy contracts) subject to underlying documentary evidence and SARB exposure limit reporting.

NDFs are not permissible as an onshore resident hedging instrument because ZAR is legally deliverable through the authorised dealer network; only non-residents may transact NDFs offshore. The resident (Pty) Ltd therefore relies on deliverable forwards, options and authorised-dealer swaps.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a delinquent annual-return penalty per overdue period; continued non-filing triggers CIPC notice and administrative strike-off, dissolving the company and exposing directors to personal liability for acts performed during the delinquent period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements together with Audit or Independent Review Report where the Public Interest Score threshold applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders/Board; CIPC and South African Revenue Service where reporting or information requests apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of Companies Act directors' duty; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, and continued default may be referred for enforcement proceedings with administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation included with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: With Annual Return; within 30 business days after registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or false UBO data is a statutory offence; CIPC can reject the Annual Return and the company remains delinquent, leading to deregistration procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required when the Public Interest Score is 500 or more; 350-499 requires an independent review unless the company voluntarily elects a full audit. The Public Interest Score counts employees, shareholders, creditors and annual turnover as prescribed in Companies Regulations 28-29.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB or IFRS for SMEs; both are endorsed financial reporting standards under the Companies Act and are applied by South African private companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and, with each Annual Return, confirm to CIPC the current beneficial owners, including any changes arising from share transfers; failure to align the Register with actual ownership before filing makes the Annual Return defective.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of director and shareholder meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,200 per year for registered office, company secretary and CIPC submission services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 15,000 for a full IFRS audit; USD 1,500 - USD 6,000 for an independent review

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Small Business Corporation (s12E) graduated rates: 0% on first ZAR 95,000; 7% on next ZAR 350,000; 21% on next ZAR 220,000; 27% above ZAR 665,000 (turnover ceiling ZAR 20 million). Section 12C accelerated allowance of 40/20/20/20 for new manufacturing assets used directly in the die-casting process. Section 11D research and development super-deduction of 150% on approved projects. Section 18A donations deduction capped at 10% of taxable income. Employment Tax Incentive (ETI) payroll subsidy for qualifying employees.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; set-off of assessed losses capped at 80% of taxable income from 1 January 2022)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted via SARS eFiling at www.sarsefiling.co.za; provisional tax liability is managed through IRP6 estimate returns filed at six-month intervals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (ITR14) plus two provisional tax estimates (IRP6) per year for provisional taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Outer statutory deadline is 12 months after the financial year-end (s66(13), Income Tax Act 58 of 1962); the SARS eFiling 'Notice to Submit' may prescribe an earlier date; any balance of tax is payable by the due date stated on the assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-populated legal name, company registration number, SARS tax reference number and financial year commencement/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the SARS 10-digit tax number; non-resident shareholder details are not reported in this section but are disclosed in the dividend tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All local and export revenue from the sale of die-cast and tampo-printed scale replicas, including SWIFT and PayPal receipts converted to ZAR at the spot rate on receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident without a South African permanent establishment is not required to file an ITR14 for export sales; the SA payer/withholding agent remains liable for dividends tax on distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt receipts, principally foreign dividends qualifying under the s10B(2) participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the resident company return; the foreign parent relies on its domestic participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, operating expenses, s11(a) deductions, s12C manufacturing allowances and s18A donations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for cross-border management fees, royalties or service charges require transfer pricing documentation when aggregate related-party transactions exceed ZAR 5 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward under s20; only 80% of taxable income may be relieved, with the remaining 20% carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are entity-specific and cannot be transferred to or claimed by non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the 27% headline rate; reduced SBC rates (0%/7%/21%/27%) apply only where s12E status is confirmed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on retained profits; only distributions attract dividends tax at 20% or the applicable treaty rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits under s6quat for foreign withholding taxes on export royalties or interest, supported by tax certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident cannot claim s6quat credits on the SA return; treaty relief is secured through the withholding declaration process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First and second IRP6 provisional tax payments offset against the assessed normal tax to arrive at the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No IRP6 credit is claimable by non-residents; dividends tax is final at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section H - Connected Person and TP Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of connected-person cross-border transactions and acknowledgment of transfer pricing documentation obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent should ensure contemporaneous Local File/Master File records are in place before the ITR14 is lodged to avoid s31 adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fixed-amount penalty under TAA s210: ZAR 250 for the first month, rising to ZAR 500 per month thereafter, capped at 35 months; understatement penalties of 10%-150% under s222/223 depending on conduct; daily interest at the prescribed rate under s187; criminal fine and/or imprisonment up to 2 years for failure to submit a return under s234.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the paying SA company, before the dividend is paid, the SARS prescribed declaration ('Declaration by Beneficial Owner' completed via eFiling) together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence. The company retains these documents for five years, files the dividend tax return and remits the reduced-rate withholding tax to SARS within 30 days of the dividend payment. If the documents are absent at payment date, 20% is withheld and the excess is refundable only through a directed assessment by SARS.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory withholding under s49B, typically reduced to 0%-12% under an applicable DTA. Interest: 15% statutory withholding under s50B, typically reduced to 0%-10% (e.g., 0% under the SA-US DTA); s50D statutory exemptions apply to qualifying interest paid to certain financial institutions and debt instruments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds ZAR 5 million per year of assessment; Master File additionally required where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds ZAR 1 billion and those transactions exceed ZAR 50 million; Country-by-Country Report mandatory where group consolidated turnover is at least ZAR 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not impose a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as found in offshore financial centres. Substance requirements are, however, embedded in the South African residence test (place of effective management), the CFC attribution rules (s9D), the GAAR (s80A-80L) and the beneficial-ownership condition for treaty relief. The (Pty) Ltd must evidence physical premises, employees, board control, contracts, operational assets and decision-making in South Africa; a shell-like structure will be recharacterised and treaty benefits denied.
